sentences.text:
These MFAs, coming on for admission, this day, the court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT MFA No. 2124/2017 is filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation ('KSRTC' for brevity) for reducing the compensation amount as well as challenging the negligence attributed to the driver of the KSRTC bus.
MFA No. 10151/2018 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts:
The claimants are the wife, son and daughter of One N.P.Subbegowda.

That on 18.07.2015 at about 4.00 p.m., when the deceased Subbegowda was proceeding on his motor bike bearing registration No.KA-41-Q-9430 near A.Cholenahalli Village on Mysore-Channarayapatna Road, driver of KSRTC bus bearing registration No.
KA-13-F- 0091 drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motor bike, as a result of the said impact Subbegowda died at the spot.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation.
The deceased was an agriculturist and doing animal husbandry work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The claimants who are the wife and children were depending upon the earning of the deceased.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.13,35,000/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The Tribunal held the driver of the KSRTC bus was negligent in driving the bus.

4. The Tribunal has awarded compensation to the claimants as under : -

petitioner Loss of Estate to petitioners 2 and 3 Rs.30,000/-

Towards funeral and obsequies 4 ceremony and transportation of Rs.25,000/-
 dead body  Total Rs.13,35,000/-

5. The learned counsel appearing for the KSRTC submitted that the KSRTC bus driver was not rash and negligent in driving the bus, the Tribunal erroneously has fastened the entire liability on the KSRTC.
Therefore he prays for modification of the judgment with regard to rash and negligent aspect.
Also submitted that the Tribunal was in error in applying parameters in determining the compensation.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in on the higher side and therefore prays for reducing the same.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants submitted that the driver of the KSRTC bus was rash and negligent and hence the Tribunal has correctly fastened the liability on the KSRTC.

Further submitted the quantum of compensation awarded is on the lesser side and therefore prays for enhancement of the same.
7.
In the present case, when the deceased was riding a motor bike, the driver of the KSRTC bus came in a negligent manner and dashed against him.
The claimants are wife and children.
The Tribunal has fastened the entire negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.

The FIR, complaint,
charge sheet, spot mahazar, all show that the deceased was riding the motor bike on his correct side,
but the driver of the KSRTC bus had dashed the deceased's motor bike.
Charge sheet is laid against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
In this regard in the complaint also the negligence is attributed to the driver of the bus.
Therefore on this aspect, the Tribunal is right in holding that the driver of the KSRTC bus was completely rash and negligent in driving the bus and caused the accident.
Therefore there cannot be any contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Accordingly, I confirm the Tribunal's decision on issue No.1 in holding that the driver of the bus was rash and negligent in causing the accident.
8. The accident was caused on 18.7.2015.
The deceased was aged 48 years.
The Tribunal has taken monthly income at Rs.10,000/-.

The RTC extracts, certificate issued by Milk Producer Cooperative Society and the cash bill proves by preponderance of probability that the deceased was having an income more than the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The deceased was an agriculturist and supplying milk to the society.
Thus, the tribunal is correct in taking the income as Rs.10,000/- per month.

According to the age of the deceased, 25% of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC Divisional Controller vs Smt. Bhagyamma on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103293545/

sentences.text: The Tribunal has committed an error in deducting 1/4th amount towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The claimants are wife and children.

Even though the children are major,
the wife and the children were dependent on the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd income can be deducted towards personal and living expenses considering the size of the family.
As per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corpn And Another [AIR 2009 SC 3104], the applicable multiplier is '13'.

Hence, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,30,000/-

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :-
ORDER i. MFA No. 2124/2017 filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation and MFA No.
- 11 - 10151/2018 filed by the claimants are allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 25.10.2016 passed by the 4th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Hassan District (Sit at Channarayapatna), in MVC No.
1648/2015 is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,30,000/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
